questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code builds SQL from request input? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
The sort column is validated against SORTABLE_COLUMNS and inserted with sql.Identifier rather than being passed as a %(sort)s parameter. Why is a parameter not an option here?
choices: Bound parameters stand in for values, not identifiers, so ORDER BY %(sort)s would sort by a constant string and not by the column
psycopg does not support parameters in queries that have an ORDER BY clause
Parameters are slower than identifiers for sorting
sql.Identifier lets the database cache the plan for every possible column

questions.prompt: The search text becomes the parameter "%" + escape_like(query.text) + "%". What would happen if escape_like were removed but the value still passed as a bound parameter?
choices: The query would be vulnerable to SQL injection through the search box
The query would raise a syntax error whenever the text contains a percent sign
The text would be matched as a literal substring regardless of its characters
Users could still not break out of the statement, but % and _ typed into the search box would act as wildcards and could match more rows than intended

questions.prompt: What stops an administrator from one tenant listing users that belong to another tenant by tampering with query-string parameters?
choices: escape_like removes tenant identifiers from the search text
The role filter limits results to the caller's own roles
tenant_id is taken from g.auth and is always the first clause of the WHERE, so no query-string parameter can remove or replace it
The deleted_at IS NULL clause hides rows from other tenants
